correctness.rationale: A nonconstant unital multiplicative monoid morphism between prime-power residue monoids must preserve the source zero: its target zero image is an idempotent, and the only target idempotents are 0,1; image 1 forces the morphism to be constant one. In the paper’s nonconstant parameterization ψ([p]^u[b])=[q]^{uv}[r]^u φ([b]) with r and φ(unit) invertible, ψ([p]^e)=0 forces [q]^{ev}=0 modulo q^f, equivalent to ev≥f, hence v≥ceil(f/e). The printed v≥floor(f/e) retains an impossible nondivisible bottom stratum. For p=q=3,e=2,f=3 the displayed floor model counts 55 parameters; removing v=1 leaves corrected 19. Explicit v=1,r=1,trivial-unit example sends source 0 to 9 mod27, invalid. Independently enumerated all 19 distinct unital multiplicative maps Z/9→Z/27 via 2,3 generator images and all 81 multiplication-table identities; 18 are nonconstant and one constant one. Finite count supports concrete example only, while general threshold follows the symbolic zero-element argument.

The unital nonconstant versus constant-one distinction is necessary; a zero-preserving assumption cannot be silently dropped.
